title: Anthropic Co-Founder to Make 'Large Gift' to Trump Accounts, Bessent Says
excerpt: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent disclosed the coming gift on CNBC a day after Anthropic's $93.5 billion IPO. Reuters identified the founder as Tom Brown; the amount has not been disclosed.
body:
• Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CNBC on November 20 that an Anthropic founder will make a "large gift" to Trump Accounts "over the next few weeks" — he named neither the founder nor the amount.
  • Reuters, citing a source familiar with the donation, identified the founder as Tom Brown, Anthropic's co-founder and chief compute officer.
  • The announcement came a day after Anthropic's IPO raised $93.5 billion, including the underwriters' option — the context for the gift, not its size, which remains undisclosed.
  • For parents: Trump Accounts give US citizens born between 2025 and 2028 a one-time $1,000 Treasury deposit; any child under 18 with a Social Security number can hold an account. Details are at TrumpAccounts.gov.

An Anthropic co-founder is preparing a large donation to Trump Accounts, the federal investment accounts for children, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on CNBC on Friday, November 20. "One of the Anthropic founders is going to make a large gift to Trump Accounts over the next few weeks," Bessent said, according to Reuters. "We believe that it's important for these great entrepreneurs to share their bounty." Bessent did not name the founder or give a figure. Reuters, citing a source familiar with the donation, identified the founder as Tom Brown, Anthropic's co-founder and chief compute officer, in its fuller report carried by the Los Angeles Post.

What is known — and what is not

Two things are confirmed: a gift is coming within weeks, and the Treasury is presenting it as large. Everything else about it — the amount, whether it comes from Brown personally or through a foundation, and which children's accounts it would reach — has not been disclosed. The largest benchmark in the programme so far is Michael and Susan Dell's pledge of $250 for each of 25 million children, a commitment estimated at $6.25 billion; there is no basis yet to place the Anthropic gift anywhere on that scale, and it should not be reported as comparable until terms are announced.

Why the timing matters

The announcement landed one day after Anthropic's stock market debut raised $93.5 billion, including the underwriters' exercised option to buy additional shares — a listing that turned the company's founders into some of the wealthiest people in technology overnight. Trump Accounts have become the administration's chosen vehicle for that new wealth to be seen flowing toward children: more than 100 companies, states and philanthropists have pledged matching contributions or gifts, among them the Dells, Ray and Barbara Dalio, and SpaceX president Gwynne Shotwell.

How Trump Accounts work

Trump Accounts are tax-advantaged investment accounts for US children under 18 with a Social Security number. Children born between January 1, 2025, and December 31, 2028, receive a one-time $1,000 deposit from the Treasury. Families and others can add contributions within an annual cap, and charitable and government contributions sit outside that cap. For diaspora families in the US, eligibility turns on the child's citizenship and Social Security number, not on the parents' visa status — but the $1,000 seed is limited to the 2025–2028 birth window. Parents can check their child's position and claim an account through TrumpAccounts.gov.

What to watch next

The gift itself: its size, structure and eligibility rules, expected within the next few weeks. Until Brown or Anthropic announces terms, the confirmed story is the commitment, not a number.
